November 26, 1940.

The Shanghai Chinese Power Company - seizure of
archives by Japanese Gendarmerie.

The Shanghai Chinese Power Company, formerly
located in Nantao, has been maintaining an office
at No. 502 Rue Lafayette, French Concession, since
the outbreak of local hostilities in 1937. A number
of meters, machinery parts, documents, and account
books of the Company were kept at this address in
charge of some 10 employees.

At 11.30 a.m. on November 23, four Japanese
Gendarmes in plain clothes, accompanied by members
of the French Police, visited the office of the
Chinese Power Company, 502 Rue Lafayette, and conducted
a thorough search of the premises. On leaving, the
Japanese Gendarmes took away the documents, account
books and two keys for the safes and also warned the
inmates against removing anything from the premises.

A Chinese Detective of the French Police is now
on observation duty at the above address while the
employees still remain on the premises.
page_data.zh:
1940年11月26日。

上海华商电气公司——日本宪兵队查封档案。

上海华商电气公司原址位于南市，自1937年本地战事爆发以来，一直在法租界霞飞路502号设有办事处。该公司的一批电表、机器零件、文件和账簿存放于此地址，由约10名员工负责看管。

11月23日上午11时30分，四名便衣日本宪兵在法国警察的陪同下，视察了位于霞飞路502号的华商电气公司办事处，并对该场所进行了彻底搜查。离开时，日本宪兵带走了文件、账簿以及两个保险箱钥匙，并警告屋内人员不得从该场所移除任何物品。

目前，一名法国警局的华籍侦探正在上述地址执行监视任务，公司员工仍留在该场所内。

page_data.en:
Chinese Company
Taken Over

Chinese Power Offices
In French Concession
Seized by New Regime

Indignation over the seizure by the Japanese and new Chinese officials of the Shanghai Chinese Electric Company's branch office in the French Concession (on Saturday), described as a purely private Chinese commercial enterprise, was expressed yesterday in Chinese press report appearing in the "National Herald" and "Chinese American Daily News." Chinese in the Concession are said to be trembling with fear as the authorities in the Concession cannot give protection to private enterprises.

The office was taken over at 11.20 a.m. when the Japanese and new Chinese officials occupied the office building at 502 Avenue Dubail near Rue Lafayette. The French police, the reports state, did not prevent the Japanese from taking over the property. Chinese employees in the office were forced to surrender their documents and the keys for opening the safe. Although the employees were allowed to leave, they were not allowed to take away their personal belongings, the reports allege.

Only Skeleton Staff

The office thus taken over by the Japanese is said to be one of the biggest Chinese power companies, with head offices formerly located in Nantao. This company ran the tramway service and supplied electricity in Chinese territory before the hostilities. After the hostilities had spread to Nantao, the business had to be closed and workers dismissed.

Despite difficulties, however, the company managed to supply electricity to the church area in Siccawei until the French police evacuated the area in favour of the Japanese. It was because of this Siccawei business that the company still kept an office in the French Concession. After the French withdrawal from the Siccawei area, only a skeleton staff was maintained in the Chinese office until the Japanese occupation, according to the reports.

华商公司
被接管

法租界内的
华商电力办事处
被新政权查封

据《国民新闻报》和《中美日报》刊登的中文媒体报道，昨日有人对日本人及新中国官员查封上海华商电气公司位于法租界的分公司（于周六发生）表示愤慨，该公司被描述为一家纯粹的私营华商企业。据报道，租界内的华人因当局无法保护私营企业而惊恐万分。

报道称，上午11时20分，日本人和新中国官员占领了靠近霞飞路的杜美路502号的办公大楼，接管了该办事处。法国警察并未阻止日本人接管财产。办事处的中国雇员被迫交出文件和开启保险箱的钥匙。报道声称，虽然允许雇员离开，但不允许他们带走个人财物。

仅留留守人员

据报道，被日本人接管的这家办事处属于最大的华商电力公司之一，其总公司原位于南市。在战事发生前，该公司在华界地区经营电车服务并供应电力。战事蔓延至南市后，业务被迫停止，工人被遣散。

然而，尽管困难重重，该公司仍设法向徐家汇教堂区域供电，直到法国警察将该区域移交给日本人为止。正是因为徐家汇的业务，该公司才在法租界保留了一个办事处。据报道，在法国人撤离徐家汇地区后，华人办事处仅维持少量留守人员，直至被日本人占领。

Cheng Yien Pao, Chinese-American Daily News, National Herald,
Shun Pao and Sin Wan Pao :-

JAPANESE TAKE OVER NANTAO TRAMWAY AND ELECTRICITY COMPANY

Following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in 1937, the Nantao Tramway and Electricity Co.
suspended operations. When the hostilities ceased in Shanghai,

the management still found it impossible to resume operations
whereupon an office was established at House No. 502 Rue
Lafayette to deal exclusively with the liquidation of the
firm.

Unexpectedly, at 11.20 a.m. yesterday more
than ten Japanese together with members of a certain party
arrived at the office in two motor cars and declared that
they had come to "take over" the office. Some ten detectives
and uniformed men of the French Police who were present did
not interfere.

The members of the office could do nothing
but hand over all the documents and keys of the safe to the
callers who left about 1 p.m.

Detectives of the French Police have been
left on the premises. The office staff were allowed to leave
the premises but they were not allowed to take away their
personal belongings.

《诚言报》、《中美日报》、《国民新闻报》、
《申报》和《新闻报》：-

日本人接管南市电车与电力公司

继1937年中日战事爆发后，南市电车与电力公司
停止运营。当上海战事平息时，

管理层发现仍无法恢复运营，
于是便在霞飞路502号设立了一个办事处，专门处理
公司的清算事宜。

出乎意料的是，昨天上午11时20分左右，
十多名日本人连同某党派成员
乘坐两辆汽车抵达该办事处，宣称他们是来“接管”办事处的。当时在场的约十名法国警察侦探和制服警员
未加干涉。

办事处人员别无选择，只能将所有文件和保险箱钥匙交给
来访者，后者于下午1点左右离开。

法国警察侦探已留守在该场所。办事处职员被允许离开
该场所，但不允许带走他们的个人财物。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I, Special Branch
REPORT
File No. S. B. Reg. No. 1234
Date June 28, 19 38.

Subject Chinese Electric Power Company - ex-employees call
at Company's Office.

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by [Signature]

Some 60 ex-employees of the Chinese Electric Power
Company, Nantao, called at the company's office, Room 254
Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Building, The
Bund, at 10 a.m. June 27 and requested the issue of the
remaining one-third of the annual bonus for the year 1937.
Mr. Sung Ts-fee (孫志飛 ), Chief of the Personnel
Department, interviewed the callers and informed them that
as a result of the assassination of Koo Shing-ih, Chairman
of the Board of Directors, the matter had been temporarily
shelved, and that the Board would convene a meeting to
appoint a new chairman when he would be requested to deal
with their demands. He further informed the ex-employees
that they might call again at the office on July 3 for
information, whereupon the callers withdrew.

During the course of the interview, Mr. Sung Ts-
fee showed the callers a letter that he had received from
the Board of Directors of the Company. The letter contains
the following two points :-

1. That the compromise reached in connection with the
issue of retiring gratuities be maintained.

2. That the issue of the remaining one-third of the annual
bonus must be in accordance with the compromise already
reached.

C. 28/6

D. S.
[Signature: Da. Pitts.]

D. C. (Special Branch)

日期 1938年6月28日。

主题 华商电气公司——前雇员前往公司办事处。

撰写人 D.S. Pitts 转呈人 [签名]

约60名原籍南市的华商电气公司前雇员，于6月27日上午10时来到外滩汇丰银行大楼254室的公司办事处，要求发放1937年度剩余的三分之一年终奖金。人事部主管孙志飛先生（Mr. Sung Ts-fee）会见了来访者，并告知他们，由于董事会主席顾馨一（Koo Shing-ih）遇刺身亡，此事暂时搁置，董事会将召开会议任命新主席，届时将请新主席处理他们的诉求。他还告知前雇员，他们可于7月3日再次到办事处询问消息，随后来访者离去。

在会谈过程中，孙志飛先生向来访者展示了他收到的一封来自公司董事会的信函。信函包含以下两点：-

1. 维持关于发放退休酬金达成的妥协方案。

2. 剩余三分之一年终奖金的发放必须依据已达成的妥协方案进行。

C. 28/6

D. S.
[签名: Da. Pitts.]

Date July 5, 19 38.

Subject Chinese Electric Power Company - Situation

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. **〔此处转录不清〕**

During the morning of July 4, about forty
ex-employees of the Chinese Electric Power Company
interviewed Mr. Sung Tse-fee, Chief of the Personnel
Department, in the directors' office, Room 254, Hongkong
and Shanghai Bank Building, The Bund, in connection with
their demands for the payment of annual bonus and the
re-issue of a loan of one month's wages. Mr. Sung told
them that Mr. Chu Chi-ling (朱季琳), who has been
recently appointed Chairman of the Standing Committee of
the Board of Directors, is of the opinion that the
question of their dismissal had already been settled,
and that consequently there was no ground for the
ex-employees to conduct further agitation. Tseu Kwang-
yung (周光榮), one of the labour delegates, later
communicated direct with Mr. Chu Chi-ling by telephone,
but it is said that the demands of the ex-employees were
definitely rejected, and they were censured for causing
a nuisance. The callers eventually dispersed in an
orderly manner.

It is reported that the ex-employees will appeal
to the French Police this morning, July 5, and intend to
call at the residence of Mr. Chu Chi-ling, Rue Victor
Emmanuel III.

It is also reported that the directors' office
will shortly be removed to the French Concession, a part
of the documents having already been taken to the home
of Mr. Chu Chi-ling.

D.C. (Special Branch).

Ja. Pitts.
D. S.

7月4日上午，约四十名华商电气公司前雇员在外滩汇丰银行大楼254室的董事办公室会见了人事部主管孙志費先生（Mr. Sung Tse-fee），就支付年终奖金和重新发放一个月工资贷款的要求进行交涉。孙先生告诉他们，最近被任命为董事会常务委员会主席的朱季琳先生（Mr. Chu Chi-ling）认为，他们的解雇问题已经解决，因此前雇员没有理由继续进行煽动活动。劳工代表之一的周光榮（Tseu Kwang-yung）后来直接通过电话与朱季琳先生联系，据说前雇员的要求被明确拒绝，并因制造麻烦而受到谴责。来访者最终有序散去。

Made by D. S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford

During the morning of June 20, about eighty
ex-employees of the Chinese Electric Power Company called
at the directors' office, Room 254, Hongkong and Shanghai
Bank Building, The Bund, with a view to securing a reply
in connection with their demands for the issue of the
remaining one-third of the annual bonus. Five of them
acting as representatives were received by Mr. Sung Tse-fee,
Chief of the Personnel Department and Mr. Loh Zoong-ling,
Chief of the Traffic Department; they were told that their
requests had been rejected and that the Board of Directors
had published a notice to this effect in the Sin Wan Pao
(Vide Special Branch Report dated 20/6/38). The labour
delegates, however, insisted on the payment of the bonus,
and submitted a further demand for the re-issue of the
loan of one month's pay which was granted after the
outbreak of local Sino-Japanese hostilities in August,
1937 and was not due to be refunded until 1941 but which
actually had been deducted from the retiring gratuities
distributed to them during May, 1938. The management's
representatives promised to refer this request to the
Board and give a reply on June 24.

REPORT
Date June 7, 1936.
Subject Chinese Electric Power Company - Situation
Made by D.S. Fitts Forwarded by C Crawford. i. 9.

During the morning of June 6, twelve ex-employees
of the Chinese Electric Power Company called at the
directors' office, Room 254, Hongkong and Shanghai Bank
Building, The Bund, and submitted a letter to the Board
of Directors applying for payment of the remaining
one-third of the unpaid annual bonus, equivalent to
20 days' wages. In reply, Mr. Loh Zoong-ling (陸仲麟),
Chief of the Traffic Department and representative of the
management, stated that the request had already been
conveyed to the Board of Directors which is of the opinion
that no further demands could be accepted as the services
of ex-employees had been dispensed with and that the
question of payment of the 20 days' annual bonus would be
taken up only if and when the company resumed business.
Nevertheless, Mr. Loh told them that he would refer the
letter to the Board, and give a reply on June 13.

Enquiries made among ex-employees indicate that
they still are unwilling to accept the procedure concerning
their dismissal, and are strongly opposed to the retention
of the services of seventy-two clerks and five workers.
This particular point was mentioned in the letter in which
they demand payment of wages to all ex-employees as a
palliative measure.

It is reported that the ex-employees intend to
demand the issue of superannuation for work performed
prior to 1931, but for the time being, they will not
submit any further demands until the dispute regarding
the annual bonus is settled.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 7 JUNE 1936 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

制作人：D.S. Fitts 转呈人：C Crawford. i. 9.

6月6日上午，十二名中国电力公司前雇员前往外滩汇丰银行大楼254室董事办公室，向董事会提交了一封信，申请支付剩余未付的年终奖金的三分之一，相当于20天的工资。作为答复，交通部主任兼管理层代表陸仲麟 (Loh Zoong-ling) 先生表示，该请求已转达董事会，董事会认为不能再接受进一步的要求，因为前雇员的雇佣关系已解除，只有在公司恢复营业时才会处理支付20天年终奖金的问题。尽管如此，陸先生告诉他们，他会将这封信转交董事会，并于6月13日给予答复。

对前雇员的调查显示，他们仍然不愿意接受有关解雇的程序，并强烈反对留用七十二名职员和五名工人。他们在信中特别提到了这一点，并要求向所有前雇员支付工资作为一种缓和措施。

据报道，前雇员打算要求发放1931年之前工作期间的退休金，但暂时在年终奖金纠纷解决之前，他们不会提出进一步的要求。

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford

During the morning of June 3, about fifty
ex-workers of the Chinese Electric Power Company called
at the directors' office, Room 254, Hongkong and Shanghai
Bank Building, The Bund. Twenty of them entered the
office and put forward two demands :-

1. That the money deducted from the wages of ex-workers
during October and November, 1937 for the purchase
of Liberty Bonds (equal to 5% of their monthly pay)
be refunded.

2. That the special bonus equivalent to 20 days'
pay which, it is alleged, the management had
promised during the course of negotiation in
November, 1937, be issued.

In reply, the Company accepted the first demand,
but rejected the second, as it was groundless. The
workers stated that they would continue negotiation on
June 6.

Tseu Yuin-kiang (周云江) and Woo Siang-ming
(吴湘明), the two labour delegates of the Chinese
Electric Power Company, who left for Hongkong on April 28
to interview Mr. Tu Yueh-sung, returned on May 15 by the
s.s. "Empress of Russia". They stated that since Mr. Tu
was in Hankow, they had failed to carry out their mission
to discuss ways and means of bringing about a settlement
of the dispute.

of the ex-employees now appear to have abandoned further
agitation against their dismissal. Up to May 16, a
total of 688 ex-employees had been paid retiring
gratuities and superannuation amounting to $199,140.55.

Following the receipt of a cable from Mr. Tu Yueh-sung

Bank Building. During the course of this meeting, a set

the issue of retiring gratuities to the employees whose

Notification dated May 8, issued by the Chinese
Electric Power Company in regard to the distribution
of retiring gratuities and superannuation.

1. In compliance with the demands of the workers, the
Board of Directors has decided to increase the amount
of retiring gratuities from one month's salary, which
has been already granted, to three months' pay, and in
an effort to generally assist the workers, these retiring
gratuities will be paid in one lump sum.

2. Superannuation, calculated up to November 1937 only,
will be issued with the gratuities and all debts due
to the company shall be deducted therefrom.

3. Workers are required to have completed any unfinished
tasks prior to receiving their money, for which they
should call personally at the appointed time and place.

4. Should the company be in a position in the future
to resume operations, the services of the now retiring
workers will be first solicited.

5. The decision reached on February 23, in regard to
the distribution of retiring gratuities, is hereby
cancelled.

6. Workers are requested to call personally for the
monies due them between May 10 and 17, 1938 at the
offices of Mr. Lee Ioong Tsoh (李永祚), Chartered
Accountant, in the Hung Li Building, 459 Honan Road
(corner of Tientsin Road).

Signed: Board of Directors of the
Chinese Electric Power
Company.

中国电力公司于5月8日发布的关于分发遣散费和养老金的通知。

1. 应工人的要求，董事会决定将遣散费金额从已发放的一个月工资增加到三个月工资，并且为了普遍援助工人，这些遣散费将一次性支付。

2. 养老金仅计算至1937年11月，将与遣散费一并发放，并从中扣除欠公司的所有债务。

3. 工人在领取款项前需完成任何未完成的任务，为此他们应在指定时间和地点亲自前往。

4. 如果公司未来有能力恢复运营，将优先聘用目前离职的工人。

5. 此前于2月23日作出的关于分发遣散费的决定 hereby 取消。

6. 请工人于1938年5月10日至17日期间，亲自前往河南路459号（天津路转角）恒利大楼内特许会计师李永祚（Lee Ioong Tsoh (李永祚)）的办公室领取应得款项。

Date April 28, 1938.
Subject Chinese Electric Power Company - Nantao
Made by D.S. Pitts    Forwarded by C. Gustafson

Dissension is still reported to exist among the
former employees of the Chinese Electric Power Company.
The majority are opposed to the decision of the management
to dispense with their services and insist upon the
resumption of negotiations on the return from Hongkong
of Mr. Sung Tse-fee, Chief of the Personnel Department
and a representative of the management. About 150
workers formerly attached to the Mechanical Department,
however, are said to be willing to sever connections with
the company, and have openly expressed their views in
this connection to their labour delegates. Consequently,
the labour delegates will discuss the matter with Mr. Chu
Yee-sung (朱怡聲), son of Mr. Chu Chi-ling, a member
of the Board of Directors, at his office, No.42 Rue du
Consulat.

It is also reported that some 100 ex-employees of
the company have registered with the Japanese authorities
through the Nantao Autonomous Commission, but only thirty
mechanics have been given employment in the electric plant
of the company at Nantao which is being partially operated
by the Japanese military.

（印章：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER (DIVISIONS) / 25 APR. 1938）

At 9.30 a.m. to-day, April 25, about fifty former
employees of the Chinese Electric Power Company appeared
in the directors' office, Room 254, Hongkong and Shanghai
Bank Building, The Bund, to await the arrival of their
representatives and responsible members of the management.

It is learned that Mr. Sung Tse-fee, Chief of the
Personnel Department and one of the representatives of
the management, left for Hongkong on April 22 with a view
to soliciting the opinion of Mr. Tu Yueh-sung in order to
effect a settlement of the existing dispute.

During the afternoon of April 23, four delegates
of the ex-employees visited French Police Headquarters
in answer to a call; they were warned to maintain peace
and order and to advise their colleagues not to hold any
gatherings. Subsequently, two detectives of the French
Police and the four labour delegates interviewed lawyer
Chu Yee-sung (朱治聲), son of Mr. Chu Chi-ling
(朱季琳), a member of the Board of Directors, in his
office, 42 Rue du Consulat, and enquired about the
decision of the Board in connection with the demands of
the employees. Mr. Chu stated that the Board had
definitely decided to dispense with the services of the
employees, and that, unless the men agreed to make
certain concessions, he would not mediate in the dispute.

REPORT
Date April 14, 19 38.

Subject Chinese Electric Power Company - Nantao

Made by D.S. Pitts    Forwarded by [Signature]

Negotiations between the management and ex-employees
of the Chinese Electric Power Company remain at a standstill.
Information has been obtained to the effect that
the "Nantao Autonomous Commission" is conducting registration
of the former employees of the company, and notices to this
effect were posted in Nantao on April 11. One Tsang
Zah-neu (张若愚), ex-inspector No.19, who is connected
with the People's Livelihood Section of the Commission, is
in charge of the registration, but up to the present, only
about twenty ex-employees are said to have registered with
this bogus organization. It is reported that the
Commission intends to restore public utility services in
Nantao under the auspices of the Japanese authorities.
So far the electric lights have been partially restored
for the use of Japanese troops, but there is no indication
of an immediate resumption of the tramway service in view
of many prevailing difficulties. Further, the trolley
wires damaged during the hostilities have not yet been
repaired.

A "Water and Electric Service Section" of the
Bureau of Communications of the Shanghai Dah Dao City
Government has been formed with an office at Room 29,
Yokohama Specie Bank Building, 24 The Bund. About seven
Japanese and Chinese are working in this office which is
engaged in making investigations into the properties of
the Chinese waterworks and electric companies in Chapei
and Nantao.

华商电气公司管理层与前雇员之间的谈判仍处于停滞状态。已获得消息表明，“南市自治委员会”正在对该公司前雇员进行登记，相关通知已于4月11日在南市张贴。与该委员会民生部有关的前第19号督察张若愚（Tsang Zah-neu）负责登记工作，但截至目前，据说只有约二十名前雇员在这个伪组织登记。据报道，该委员会意图在日本当局的支持下恢复南市的公用事业服务。目前电灯已部分恢复供日军使用，但由于存在许多困难，尚无迹象表明电车服务会立即恢复。此外，战事期间受损的电车线尚未修复。

上海大道市政府交通局下设“水电服务科”，办公地点设在外滩24号横滨正金银行大楼29室。约有七名中日人员在该办公室工作，该部门正致力于调查闸北和南市的华商水厂和电气公司的财产状况。

that the Board was of the opinion that there was no room
for further discussion in this connection on the grounds

agreements might possibly be held valid if and when the
company resumed business. The labour delegates
considered that this statement was too vague, and
suggested that each of the ex-employees be issued a note
bearing the amount of superannuation due to him, and that
those who applied for the fund should be granted half of
the amounts standing to their credit, while the remaining
sums should be deposited with the company. Mr. Sung
promised to refer the suggestion to the Board, and
indefinitely postponed the meeting.

dissatisfied with Mr. Sung Tse-fee for his alleged
pro-management attitude. He was formerly considered

During the morning of April 7, the fifth meeting

the Chinese Electric Power Company took place in the
directors' office, Room 254, Hongkong and Shanghai Bank
Building, The Bund. About fifty ex-employees in
addition to their four representatives were present.
Throughout the conference, the subject matter under
discussion was a reiteration of the demands of the
workers, requiring the Board to assure their reinstatement
if and when the company resumed business, and to maintain
all agreements concluded between labour and capital.
Mr. Sung Tse-fee, Chief of the Personnel Department and
one of the management's delegates, informed the labour
representatives that with regard to the first demand, the
Board had agreed to preferentially engage them if the
company re-opened, but definitely refused to hold as
valid all labour agreements. The employees expressed
satisfaction with the reply in connection with the first
demand, and decided to hold a further meeting on April 9
in an endeavour to bring about a settlement of the

During the forenoon of April 4, a meeting was held
in the directors' office of the Chinese Electric Power
Company, Room 254, Hongkong and Shanghai Bank Building,
The Bund, when four representatives of the former employees
and four members of the management were present. Mr. Sung
Tse-fee, Chief of the Personnel Department and one of the
representatives of the management, informed the employees'
delegates that the Board had agreed to grant them a
retiring gratuity in a lump sum equivalent to one and
half months' pay, instead of one month's, provided that
the ex-employees recognize its decision concerning their
dismissal. In reply, the employees' delegates stated
that if the Board guaranteed to reinstate all ex-employees
when the company resumed business and to hold as valid
all agreements concluded between labour and capital, they
would be willing to continue discussions with the management
for a satisfactory settlement. Mr. Sung then suggested
that these proposals be referred to the Board and postponed
the next meeting until April 7.

With regard to the closing down of the company's
office at No.7 Rue Montauban (Vide Special Report 4/4/38),
a number of the former employees allege that the action
was pre-arranged by the Board in conjunction with the
landlords, apparently for the purpose of preventing them
from utilising it as a communication address.

5.

Re trouble with employees of the Chinese Electric
Power Co., No. 12 The Bund.

Sir,

At 10a.m. this inst. a further meeting between the
workers and directors of the above concern was held in
the offices at No. 12 The Bund (Room 254) when the workers
requested that compensation as well as a promise of re-
engagement (upon the resumption of business) be given
them. The directors have promised to give a definite
reply to this at 10a.m. on 7/4/38 at which time a further
meeting will be commenced.

During today's meeting the directors of the company
offered 6 weeks wages to the workers. This was neither
accepted nor refused, the workers also apparently preferring
to leave the discussion of this matter to the next
meeting.

The meeting dispersed quietly.

A further report will be forwarded in due course.

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Crawford

During the forenoon of March 30, Mr. Wong Dong-sung
(王桐生), Chief of the General Affairs Department of
the Chinese Electric Power Company, received a threatening
letter through the post, a translation of which is as
follows :-

"Tseu Pah-yu (周伯禹), Wong Pah-yu (黄伯禹),
Chen Chun-poh (陈君博) and Tsu Zoong-zung (朱重盛)!
You are traitors who should be killed. We will deal
with you by pistols. Be careful while on the streets.
Try to find better means of transportation so that
you can keep your lives intact for another few years.
If you ignore the advice of our 'chief,' your wives
will belong to others. Do you want to live or to die?
Do you like the prospect of going to Hell ? You may
believe it or not. We will make you know our strength.
"Diehard, Dong Sung, we warn you to get out of
the company, otherwise, we will present you ten rounds
of pistol ammunition, and your children will receive
the same treatment.

'Big fellow' Zee Foh-sung (大亨徐福身."

The envelope of the letter bears the following inscriptions:
"Mr. Wong Dong-sung,
Chinese Electric Power Company,
Hongkong and Shanghai Bank building,
Foochow Road.
From Loh (陆 )"

“周伯禹 (Tseu Pah-yu)、黄伯禹 (Wong Pah-yu)、陈君博 (Chen Chun-poh) 和朱重盛 (Tsu Zoong-zung)！
你们是应当被杀死的汉奸。我们将用手枪对付你们。在街上行走时要小心。设法寻找更好的交通工具，以便让你们再苟活几年。如果无视我们要‘首领’的劝告，你们的妻子将归他人所有。你们是想活还是想死？你们喜欢下地狱的前景吗？信不信由你。我们会让你们知道我们的厉害。

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be commented on by investigating officer).

At 11.20 a.m. 1-4-38 one named Zung Chuen Poh brought to the station a letter of threatening nature which was addressed to him and the four other complts and received at the offices of the Chinese Electric Power Co., Room 254, H. & S. Bank Building, at about 11 a.m. on the 30-3-38.

This letter, a translation of which is attached, alleges that the recipients are traitors and warns them that they will soon be killed. This letter is signed by "Zee Foh Sung (徐福生)" and was posted on the morning of 30-3-38 at the Rue Massenet Post Office, r.C. It states that it is intended as the first warning.

The recipients, all of whom reside in r.C. can give no information as to the writer and they do not suspect anyone. They stated that they are all friendly with the staff and have no enemies. All five complainants are employed in the Statistical Department of the Chinese Electric Power Co..

It was learnt that there is an employee of the name of "Zee Foh Sung" but except that he is a coolie none of the complainants know him by sight. Enquiries will however be made regarding this man.

The letter will be forwarded to Mr. May Yoh, the handwriting expert, for his opinion.

As all the complainants reside in r.C., they have been advised to report the matter to the French Police as well, and have been instructed to inform the Police immediately in the event of their receiving any further similar communication.

1938年4月1日上午11:20，一名叫陈启博 (Zung Chuen Poh) 的人向捕房提交了一封具有恐吓性质的信件，该信寄给他及其他四名原告，于1938年3月30日上午11点左右在华商电气公司办公室（汇丰银行大楼254室）收到。

这封信（附译文）指控收件人是汉奸，并警告他们即将被杀。此信由“徐福生 (Zee Foh Sung)”署名，并于1938年3月30日上午在法租界马思南路邮局寄出。信中称这是第一次警告。

收件人均居住在法租界，无法提供关于写信人的任何信息，也不怀疑任何人。他们表示与所有职员关系友好，没有敌人。五名原告均受雇于华商电气公司统计部。

获悉有一名员工名叫“徐福生 (Zee Foh Sung)”，但除知道他是一名苦力外，原告均不认识其相貌。不过，将对此人进行调查。

该信将转交笔迹专家梅耀 (May Yoh) 先生征求意见。

由于所有原告均居住在法租界，已建议他们也向法国警察当局报告此事，并指示他们一旦收到任何类似的进一步通信，立即通知警方。

To Tseu Pah Chong,
Wong Pah Ayuen,
Zung Chuen Foh,
Chu Zeong Yien,

You are four traitors. Killing you is necessary,
or shooting you by a pistol. Please take care when
taking a walk on the roadway. It is advisable that
you people should think of a way to live on for some
years, if not, the leader of our group will take steps
against you and your four wives will belong to somebody
else.

To Dong Sung,

Why don't you die as you are so old now?

I have to warn you that you should leave the company
immediately. If not, I will come to see you with a pistol
and 10 rounds of ammunition. Some method will be used
also against your son and daughter.

No. 1 Notice of Warning.

From Zee Foh Sung,
Big Man.

You five men will soon die. We want you five men to
die together. This is up to you people to believe it or
not.

See what colour we will show you.

第一号警告通知。

来自 徐福生 (Zee Foh Sung),
大亨。

你们五个人很快就会死。我们要你们五个人

Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by C. Crawford D.S.

Despite the repeated efforts made by the former
employees of the Chinese Electric Power Company, the
Board of Directors has given no indication of cancelling
its decision to dispense with their services. It is
reported that the Japanese authorities are effecting the
repair of the plants in Nantao with a view to restoring
the electric supply and tramway service. About 200
ex-employees comprising the mechanics, drivers and
conductors, being anxious to earn a living, are said
to be willing to serve under the Japanese management
if the Board definitely rejects their demands.

REPORT
Date March 22, 1938.

Subject Chinese Electric Power Company - Nantao

Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by C. Cranston

In connection with the decision of the Management
of the Chinese Electric Power Company to dispense with
the services of the employees, information has been
obtained to the effect that a number of the employees
intend to settle the present dispute through the Court,
and some 400 of them are said to have signed their names
agreeing to this action. The remaining employees,
however, hold a different opinion claiming that a
lengthy period will be required to settle the case
through the Court, and therefore, prefer to appoint
Mr. Sung Tse Fee, Chief of the Personnel Department,
to negotiate with the Board of Directors for the further
issue of the maintenance allowances and the retention of
their services but without pay.

The majority of the employees are dissatisfied
with the attitude of Messrs. Feng Ping-nan and Chu Chi-ling,
two members of the Board of Directors, who are alleged to
be responsible for the proposal to dispense with their
services, but it is said that they will not take any
drastic action against these two members, in view of the
possibility of interference by the Police.

At 4.30 p.m., March 12, a meeting of the Board
of Directors of the Chinese Electric Power Company took
place in the office of the company, Room 254, Hongkong
and Shanghai Bank building, The Bund, when fifteen
members were present with Mr. Koo Shing-ih presiding.
Messrs. Feng Ping-nan and Wong Yuin-pu, two members of
the Board who are reported to be responsible for the
proposal to dismiss the employees, did not attend.
After discussion, the following resolutions were passed:-

1. That an announcement be issued to answer the
queries of the employees contained in the item
published in the Sin Wan Pao on March 10.
(Vide Special Report dated 11/3/38).

2. That all the account books be handed over to a
firm of chartered accountants for scrutiny.

3. That an advertisement be issued through the medium
of the newspapers to announce that the meeting of
shareholders has been postponed pending the
examination of the accounts.

4. That a further telegram be despatched to Hongkong
asking Mr. Tu Yueh-sung to remain in the posts of
Managing-Director of the Company and member of the
Board of Directors.

5. That a conference of the chiefs of various
departments be convened, during which they will
be requested to hand over the account books in
their possession.

The meeting terminated at 6.30 p.m.

With reference to resolution No.1 mentioned
above, the following announcement was published by

The item inserted in the Sin Wan Pao on
March 10 by the employees of the Chinese Electric
Power Company appears to distort the facts. The
net profit of $500,000.00 mentioned in the previous
statement of the Board includes an outstanding account
of some $870,000.00 which the company has been unable
to collect from the consumers inasmuch as they removed
from the district. Following the outbreak of the
hostilities, the company not only ceased to obtain
income, but also paid the employees full wages for a
period of three and a half months, in addition to
three months' maintenance allowances and labour
rewards amounting to more than $400,000.00. With the
payment of various miscellaneous expenses, the net
profit was exhausted.

With regard to the $3,500,000.00, the previous
announcement clearly states that the sum refers to the
accounts for the purchase of goods and other debts,
i.e. ($970,000 deposits; $1,490,000.00 goods accounts;
$850,000 guarantee funds; and $170,000 due to the
Western District Power Company). This money was in
arrears before July, 1937, and on no account should
it be considered as the expenditure of the company
within the last six months. Why do not the employees
check the statement of accounts at the Accounting
Department, as the members of this department are
on their side.    The Board has now decided to

Subject Chinese Electric Power Company - Nantao

Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by C. Crawford

The employees of the Chinese Electric Power
Company, Nantao, published an item in the Sin Wan Pao,
to-day, March 11, demanding an explanation from the
Board of Directors with regard to the expenditure which
resulted in the company incurring a debt to the extent
of $3,500,000.00, a translation of which is as follows:-

"Your announcement published on March 8, 1938
has come to our notice, the contents of which appear
to have inverted right and wrong. Being engaged
in seeking employment, we are not in a position to
conduct arguments and senseless propaganda, as you
do while enjoying an easy life and are supported by
the company's funds. Nevertheless, the fact that
the company gained a net profit of over $500,000.00
out of the gross profit of $1,000,000.00 between
January and July, 1937, was published in the
announcement of your Board. We feel confounded
by the statement that all the profits were exhausted
between the outbreak of the "August 13th" Incident

Subject Chinese Electric Power Company - Nantao

Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by C Gaskin

A meeting of the Board of Directors of the Chinese
Electric Company (Nantao), which was scheduled to have been
held at 7 p.m. March 4 in the offices of Feng & Company,
137 Peking Road, did not materialize owing to lack of a
quorum. An informal meeting was held by five directors,
including Mr. Feng Ting Nan (冯炳南) and Mr. Koo Shing-
ih (顾馨一), and it was decided to hold a meeting of the
Board of Directors at 3 p.m. March 7 at the same address,
137 Peking Road.

Mr. Sung Tse Fee (徐志飞), Chief of the Personnel
Department of the Company, called at the French Concession
office of the concern, 7 Rue Montauban, at 9 a.m. March 4.
He left at 9.30 a.m. and called again at 11.30 a.m. In an
interview with several of the employees, Mr. Sung stated that
Mr. Feng Ting Nan had intended to resign and that the committee
formed by him to deal with the affairs of the Company
following the assassination of Mr. Loh Pak Hung would be
dissolved. He added that after the resignation of Mr. Feng
Ting Nan, Mr. Tu Yueh Sung would take the responsibility of
maintaining the livelihood of the employees by continuing
to issue maintenance allowances to them.

C.L.S.s 179, 287 and the undersigned, together with
a party of Uniform Police, attended and found that about
one hundred workers had already arrived and were interview-
ing one of the directors, Mr. Ts Kyi Ling (朱奇林). It
appears that the reason for the unrest among the employees
was the fact that ever since the disruption of work at
the Power Co. in Nantao in October 1937, the management
have paid the staff full wages although they have not been
working. Now however, owing to the fact that the capital
of the company is exhausted and no income is coming in,
it is not possible to pay the staff any longer. On
learning this the staff objected, insisting that they
should receive several months pay in lieu of notice, and
on being refused, staged this meeting.

（左侧印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / - 3 MAR. 1938 / SPECIAL BRANCH）

About 200 employees of the Chinese Electric Power
Company, Nantao, assembled in the company's office, No. 7
Rue Montauban, this morning, March 2, and held a
discussion in connection with the present dispute.
Mr. Sung Tse Fee, Chief of the Personnel Department,
was also present. He stated that in February, Mr. Wong
Yuin-gu (王雲甫), a member of the Board of Directors,
was despatched to Hongkong for the purpose of consulting
with Mr. Tu Yueh-sung on the procedure to be adopted
regarding employees. During this interview, it was
decided that the employees be granted the maintenance
allowances for a further three months with effect from
March, 1938. Contrary to this arrangement, the Board
of Directors had decided to dispense with the services
of the employees, consequently Mr. Tu Yueh-sung had
tendered his resignation from his posts. Mr. Sung Tse Fee
alleged that the decision of the Board to dismiss the
employees was made at the instigation of Mr. Feng Ping-nan
(馮炳南) with the support of Messrs. Chu Chi-ling
and Chang Wen-ping (張文柄), members of the Board of
Directors. Sung further stated that Mr. Feng Ping-nan
had obtained a loan of $300,000 from the company for the pur-
pose of repatriating the employees of the Chapei Waterworks,
of which he is the Chairman of the Board of Directors,
and added that these funds would be sufficient to maintain
the livelihood of the company's staff for ten months.

Subject Chinese Electric Power Company - Nantao

Made by D.S. McKEOWN Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.I.

On February 28, about 200 mechanics and 300
workers were paid half a month's wages as the maintenance
allowances for February, at the company's offices, Room
254, Hongkong and Shanghai Bank Building, The Bund, and
No.7 Rue Montauban.

At 10.15 a.m., March 1, information was received
from a detective of the Special Branch to the effect that
some 80 workers of the company had left the French
Concession and were proceeding to the office of the
Board of Directors, Room 254, Hongkong and Shanghai Bank
building, with the object of submitting a set of demands.
This information was conveyed to Central Station.
Uniform men and detectives were posted in the office
together with detectives from the Special Branch. The
workers duly arrived at the office, and were requested
by one of the directors named Chu Chi Ling (朱记琳)
to submit their demands in writing. At 12.15 p.m.,
Mr. T.C. Chen of the firm of Feng and Co., 137 Peking
Road, telephoned stating that the director Mr. Chu was
being held in the office against his will. Inspt. Brownrigg
(Central), D.S. Larby and D.S. McKeown attended and found
that a misunderstanding had occurred, as officers from
Central Station including D.S. Barton and F.S. Potapoff
were in the office. Mr. Chu departed forthwith and
requested that the crowd of workers numbering approximately
100 persons should be dispersed leaving a few representatives
to submit written demands. This request was carried out
without difficulty.

2月28日，约200名技工和300名工人在公司办公室（外滩汇丰银行大楼254室及蒙托邦路7号）领取了相当于半个月薪水的二月份生活维持费。

3月1日上午10时15分，接到特别处一名侦探的情报，称该公司约80名工人已离开法租界，正前往董事会办公室（外滩汇丰银行大楼254室），目的是提交一系列要求。此情报已传达至中央巡捕房。制服警员和侦探，连同特别处的侦探，已被部署在办公室内。工人们如期到达办公室，并被一位名为朱记琳的董事要求以书面形式提交要求。下午12时15分，北京路137号丰和公司（Feng and Co.）的陈先生（T.C. Chen）打电话称，朱董事被强行扣留在办公室内。布朗里格督察（中央巡捕房）、拉比副探长和麦基恩副探长随即到场，发现这是一场误会，因为包括巴顿副探长和波塔波夫高级警员在内的中央巡捕房警员当时正在办公室内。朱先生随即离开，并要求驱散约100人的工人群众，只留几名代表提交书面要求。这一要求得以顺利执行。

his views on Sung Tse Fee (沈志飛), Chief of the
Personnel of the Chinese Electric Power Company and the
course of action he might suggest.    Mr. Jobez stated
that he had instituted enquiries regarding this person,
the results of which he would communicate in due course.

On February 28, the management of the Chinese
Electric Power Company drew up a notice stating that
the services of the employees will be dispensed with
as from March 1, 1938, in accordance with a decision
reached by the Board of Directors. The notice reads
as follows :-

"Following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in August, 1938, the company ceased
to supply electricity and suspended business in
all departments, but continued to issue wages to
the employees for a period of three and half months.
At the beginning of December, 1937, the company,
being unable to resume business, proposed to dismiss
all the staff, but eventually decided to retain the
services of a few employees with pay at the rate of
70% of their original wages, and temporarily suspended
the services of the remainder at half pay in order
to enable them to maintain their livelihood or

return to their native places. This treatment
compares favourably with that accorded to the
workers employed by other public utility concerns
which closed as the result of the hostilities.
    Three months have now elapsed. In view of
financial difficulties, the company is unable to
continue the issue of maintenance allowances.
Consequently the management has decided to dispense
with the services of all employees at the end of
the current month (February), and pay them one
month's wages as retiring gratuities.    Owing to
extraordinary circumstances, the company hereby
declares null and void all agreements concluded
with the employees with the exception of that
concerning life insurance.    The huge losses
sustained by the company during the hostilities
and the difficulties foreseen in the future appear
to have been realized by the public.    The notice
is hereby issued for the information of the public."

    The employees have not yet received the formal
notice concerning their dismissal, and are now awaiting
the result of an interview between Mr. Tu Yueh-sung,
member of the Board of Directors, and Mr. Sung Tse-fee,
Chief of the Personnel Department. The latter will arrive
here from Hongkong this afternoon, February 28.    Four
representatives have been appointed by the employees to
interview Mr. Sung Tse-fee upon his arrival.

ELECTRICITY USED IN
REFUGEE ZONE

Chinese Concern Not To Pay
For Power Consumed

That the Chinese electricity works
will not be responsible for the power
consumed in the refugee zone in
Nantao is the gist of a letter sent to
the French Electricity and Tramways
Co., according to a Chinese report.
The Chinese concern, since Octo-
ber 20, had been obtaining power from
the French company for Nantao and
Pootung area at about $50,000 to
$60,000 a month, according to the
report. The sum was eventually re-
duced when Pootung was occupied
by the Japanese on November 12. The
sum paid by the Chinese concern in
October last was $20,000.
As the Chinese firm had received
no revenues for the electricity con-
sumed, negotiations were started by
Mr. Loh Pah-hung, the late managing
director, with Father Jacquinot of the
refugee zone, concerning the matter.
Before any solution could be obtained,
Mr. Loh was assassinated.
Following meetings of the directors
of the Chinese works, it was decided
that the French company should be
informed that the former would not
be responsible for the payment of the
electricity consumed in the refugee
zone beginning on Tuesday, February
15, according to the report.

难民区用电

中方机构不支付
所耗电费

据中文报道，致法国电力电车公司的一封信函主旨是，中国电力厂将不对南市难民区消耗的电力负责。据报道，自10月20日以来，该中方机构一直以每月约5万至6万美元的价格从法国公司为南市和浦东地区获取电力。当11月12日日军占领浦东后，这笔费用最终得以减少。该中方机构去年10月支付的金额为2万美元。
由于该中国公司未从所消耗的电力中获得任何收入，已故总经理罗伯洪（Loh Pah-hung）先生曾就此事与难民区的饶家驹神父（Father Jacquinot）进行谈判。
在达成任何解决方案之前，罗先生遇刺身亡。
据报道，在中国电厂董事召开会议后，决定通知法国公司，自2月15日星期二起，前者将不再负责支付难民区消耗的电力费用。

Subject (in full) Meeting held at 137 Peking Road on January 4 on the subject
                  of Nantao Power Company.

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang    Forwarded by C. Crawford

With reference to the attached report(Central misc.13/38)
stating that C.D.S. 166 attached to Special Branch attended
a meeting of the directors of the Nantao Power Company held
at 137 Peking Road, on January 4, it should be pointed out
that the Special Branch was not informed of this meeting and
therefore, no detective attached to the Special Branch was
present. There is no C.D.S. 166 attached to this branch as
reported in the attached report.

    Interrogation of C.D.S. 11 attached to Central Station,
who attended the meeting, shows that the C.D.S. in question
is attached to the Political Section of the French Police,
who was on that day assigned as a "bodyguard" to Mr. Koo
Shing Ih, one of the persons attending the meeting, whose
life has been threatened by "National Salvation" elements.

    It should be explained that on several occasions it has
come to the notice of this branch that members of the French
Police Special Branch when attending such functions have in-
timated that they were attached to the Special Branch without
making it clear to which administration they belong.

                                        Sih Tse liang
D.C.(Special Branch).                   C.D.I.

1.

Re a meeting held at 137 Peking Road
on the subject of the Nantao Power Co.

On the afternoon of 4/1/38, instructions were
received from D.C.(Crime) via C.I. Bishop i/c Central
Station to post a Chinese and foreign detective at
137 Peking Road at 3.45p.m. 4/1/38 as a meeting was to
be held at which Mr. Feng Ping Nan(馮炳南) would be
present.

C.D.S. 11 and the undersigned attended at the time
stated and learnt that the meeting was to be held at
4.30p.m., therefore returned at that time, but found that
the meeting did not commence until 5.15p.m., at which time
Mr. Feng Ping Nan and nine others attended. Mr. Feng
took the chair and a general discussion as to the
advisability or otherwise of re-opening the Nantao
Power Co. followed. The subject of the death of the
late Mr. Loh Pah Oong(陸伯鏞) was also brought up as Mr.
Feng was a great friend of the deceased.

Others present were Messrs. Koo Sing In(顧星一), Voong
Nyeu Dah(馮紐達), Yau Ts Zuh(姚子佐), Ts Jung Kiang(朱榮江),
Ts Kyi Nyung(朱季濃), Weng Bu Ts(翁步滋), Wong Yuan Foo
(黃元甫), Tsang Vung Ping(張文彬), Kye Kyi Iung(奚季雍), all
of whom are co-directors of the Nantao Power Co.

The meeting closed at 8 p.m., no untoward incident
occurring. C.D.S.166 attached to Special Branch was in
attendance.

关于1月4日在北京路137号举行的
关于南市电力公司的会议。

1938年1月4日下午，接到犯罪科副巡官（D.C.(Crime)）经由中央分局警长 Bishop 发出的指令，要求于1938年1月4日下午3点45分在北京路137号部署一名华探和一名西探，因为将举行一场冯炳南先生出席的会议。

华探员11号和本人按时到达，得知会议将于下午4点30分举行，因此于该时间返回，但发现会议直到下午5点15分才开始，届时冯炳南先生及其他九人出席。冯先生主持会议，随后就重新开放南市电力公司的适宜性与否进行了一般性讨论。已故陆伯鏞先生的死亡问题也被提出，因为冯先生是死者的挚友。

其他出席者有：顾星一先生、冯纽达先生、姚子佐先生、朱荣江先生、朱季浓先生、翁步滋先生、黄元甫先生、张文彬先生、奚季雍先生，他们均为南市电力公司的联席董事。

会议于晚上8点结束，未发生任何意外事件。隶属于特务科的华探员166号在场。

Subject Chinese Electric Power Company - arrangements for payment of
bonus money.

Made by D.S. Hocking    Forwarded by 〔此处转录不清〕

At 10 a.m., December 14, twenty representatives of
the employees of the Chinese Electric Power Company again
called at the Company's office, Room 254, Hongkong and
Shanghai Bank Building. Eight of their number were
allowed to interview the management, and after some
negotiations, the following result was arrived at:-

1. That 2/3 of the usual annual bonus be issued this year,
the remaining part to be issued when the company resumes
operations and gains profit.

2. That the pay for December, which has been advanced to
certain members of the staff, not be deducted from the
annual bonus, but be deducted from the employees "life
insurance savings."

3. That the issue of maintenance allowances be effective
from December, for a period of three months.

4. That the maintenance allowance for clerical staff be
equal to 50% of their original pay, but not less than
$30 for those whose pay is over $50 a month, and not
lower than $20 for those whose pay is below $50, the
deficit to be made good by the company.

5. That the allowance for workers be also equal to 50% of
their original pay, but not less than $15, the deficit
to be paid by the company.

6. That those employees, whose services are retained, be
paid the above mentioned allowances, in addition to
20% of their original pay.

The representatives withdrew at 12.30 p.m.
It is learned that the issue of annual bonus will take
place at the Company's office at No. 7 Rue Montauban,

事由：中国电力公司 - 关于发放奖金的安排。

制作人：D.S. Hocking    转呈人：〔此处转录不清〕

12月14日上午10时，中国电力公司雇员的二十名代表再次来到位于汇丰银行大楼254室的公司办公室。其中八人获准与管理层面谈，经过一番谈判，达成如下结果：-

1. 今年发放通常年度奖金的三分之二，剩余部分待公司恢复运营并盈利后发放。

2. 已预发给部分职员的十二月份工资，不从年度奖金中扣除，而从雇员的“人寿保险储蓄”中扣除。

3. 生活津贴自十二月起生效，为期三个月。

4. 职员的生活津贴等于其原薪的50%，但月薪超过50元者不低于30元，月薪低于50元者不低于20元，差额由公司补足。

5. 工人的津贴也等于其原薪的50%，但不低于15元，差额由公司支付。

6. 对于留用的雇员，除上述津贴外，另支付其原薪的20%。

代表们于下午12时30分离去。

At 10 a.m. on the 13/12/37 representatives of
the Chinese Electric Power Co. called at Room 254 H. &
S. Bank Building 12 The Bund, and six of their number
were allowed to interview the directors. They requested
that the decision re. reduction of staff, and monthly
allowances ranging from $15 to $30 to those whose
services are dispensed with be postponed for one month,
and that the annual bonus of two months wages be issued.
The directors refused to accede to the requests.

（批：Special Branch Copy）
A notice re issue of allowances and that 2/3rds
of the annual bonus would be issued this year was posted
outside the company's office on 13/12/37 also stating
that wages loaned to members of the staff would be deduct
ed.

At 10 a.m. 14/12/37 sixteen members of the staff
again attended the office of the company, and 8
representatives interviewed Mr. Sung Tse Pei (宋子佩)
director of the company. The following three resolu-
tions were passed:-
(1) That only 2/3rds of the usual yearly bonus be issued
and the other 1/3rd will be held by the directors until
the company resumes operations.
(2) The wages for December should not be interfered with
and same will be deducted from the superannuation fund
when it is issued to employees.

1937年12月13日上午10时，中国电力公司的代表来到外滩12号汇丰银行大楼254室，其中六人获准会见董事。他们请求将关于裁减人员的决定，以及向被解雇人员发放每月15至30元津贴的决定推迟一个月，并发放相当于两个月工资的年度奖金。董事们拒绝接受这些请求。

Subject Unrest among the employees of the Chinese Electric Power Company.

Made by D.S. Hocking Forwarded by C. Gausden

About one hundred employees of the Chinese Electric
Power Company gathered at the Company's office, Room 252-4
Hongkong & Shanghai Bank Building, at 9.45 a.m. on December
10, to await the result of a directors' meeting at which it
was to be decided when the employees were to receive compen-
sation and bonus money due to them. Up until 1 p.m. neither
Mr. Loh Pah-hung (陸伯鴻), the president, nor any members of
the board of directors had appeared whereupon the crowd dis-
persed in an orderly manner.

Staff members of the company number 250 and about 750
men comprise the body of workers. The following bulletins are
at present posted outside the company's office.

1. Notice No. 7115 dated November 30, 1937.
It is announced that the Chinese Electricity
and Waterworks Company has maintained the salaries
of its employees for the past three months. Owing to
the fact that there is no hope of resuming business,
the Board of Directors of the Company have decided
with effect from December 1 to reduce the staff, only
a skeleton staff in various sections to be retained.
Those retained will draw half pay, while those whose
services will be dispensed with, will be paid allow-
ances for three months according to the following
rate :-

In connection with the decision of the Management 
of the Chinese Electric Power Company to dispense with 
the services of the employees, information has been 
obtained to the effect that a number of the employees 
intend to settle the present dispute through the vourt, 
and some 400 of them are said to have signed their names 
agreeing to this action. The remaining employees, 
however, hold a different opinion claiming that a 
lengthy period will be required to settie the case 
through the Court, and therefore, prefer to appoint 
Mr. Sung Tse Fee, Chief of the Personnel Department, 
to negotiate with the soard of Directors for the further 
issue of the maintenance allowances and the retention of 
their services but without pay. 

The majority of the employees are dissatisfied 
with the attitude of Messrs. Feng Ping-nan and chu chi-ling, 
two members of the soard of Directors, who &re alleged to 
be responsible for the proposal to dispense with their 
services, but it is said that they will not take any 
drastic action against these two members, in view of the 
possibility of interference by the Police.
